# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26 (Bu-Vb Np26)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np26  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26  
**Title (English, from literature):** Asking for thread  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Suttaviññatti* ("Asking for thread"), cataloged as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26, is a disciplinary rule from the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic robe production. According to the rule, a Buddhist monk who solicits or asks for thread and subsequently has robe-cloth woven from it incurs an offense requiring forfeiture of the cloth (*nissaggiya*) and confession (*pācittiya*). Modern translations of the text into English include that of Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26 and Bhikkhu Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26, alongside a counterpart in the nuns' discipline (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 27). Beyond the Theravāda tradition, parallel Vinaya rules and Prātimokṣa entries are preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions across several schools, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda traditions.
